title: dedicated-gpu-pool-scheduling-autoscale-warmup-debug-breadcrumbs-19
content:
Quick breadcrumbs for incident on dedicated GPU pool autoscaler warmup / capacity thrash.
Context:
- Pool: dedicated-gpu-pool-prod (N=24 NVIDIA A100)
- Autoscaler: internal/k8s-agg-autoscaler v2.1
- Symptom: frequent scale-ups followed by immediate scale-downs causing warmup thrash and increased latency (spikes to 800-1200ms p50->p95)
- First observed: 2024-11-14 03:20 UTC, recurred multiple times.

Timeline:
2024-11-14 03:20 - first spike; noticed by SLO alerts and pod churn.
03:24 - oncall (Marcus) manually pinned pool target to min=12 max=48 to stabilize while investigating.
03:30 - confirmed pattern: new nodes come up, scheduler assigns warmup-heavy pods, autoscaler scales back before pre-warmed containers ready.

What I tried (commands + outputs):
- kubectl get hpa -n redwood | grep dedicated-gpu
  -> dedicated-gpu-hpa    12/48   ...
- kubectl describe node <new-node-id>
  -> kubelet: image-pulling, docker pull in progress, container runtime waiting.
- kubectl logs -n redwood autoscaler-agg-0
  -> "Scale down candidate: pool dedicated-gpu-pool-prod, utilization 18%, safeToRemove=true"
- kubectl get pods -n redwood -o wide | grep warmup
  -> many pods in Init: pulling or ContainerCreating

Hypotheses:
- Autoscaler is evaluating utilization before GPU prep/warmup completes (startupProbe vs readinessProbe mismatch).
- Warmup scripts (model cache preload) are running as postStart lifecycle causing readiness only after long delay; autoscaler sees low utilization and removes nodes.
- Node taints/tolerations allow scheduling on new nodes immediately but readiness happens later.

Immediate mitigations tried:
- Increased cooldown window in autoscaler config from 180s -> 600s (patched, rolled out to staging).
- Added initialDelaySeconds=120 to readinessProbe for heavy-serving pods to avoid early termination.
- Changed warmup from postStart hook to initContainer preload (faster and blocks readiness until done) - experimental in staging.
- Pinned min pool size to 24 overnight to reduce churn.

Notes / next steps:
- Add metric "warmup_ready_ratio" to console dashboards: fraction of pods that are Ready within 5m of scheduling.
- Adjust autoscaler decision logic to account for pod readiness state or presence of initContainers with warmup label.
- Re-run incident replay in staging with varying cooldowns (180/300/600) and measure cost/latency.
- Investigate if kernel offload/driver install times vary by region (reported longer in us-west2).

Relevant links:
- JIRA: INFRA-2148
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/789
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02XXXXXX/p171037XXXXXX

Raw error snippets:
- "Warning FailedCreate Pod sandbox changed"
- "Error image pull: manifest for redwood/serving:prod-20241114 not found"
- autoscaler log: "deciding scaleDown: predictedUtil 15% < threshold 30% -> scaleDown"

Questions for next oncall:
- Can we defer scale-down until all scheduled pods reach readiness or a fixed grace period?
- Should warmup be required as initContainer for all heavy models?
- Can we prioritize scheduling onto existing warmed GPUs where available (anti-affinity to new nodes)?
